title: The bottleneck has moved
lines: Artificial intelligence can produce candidate research faster than institutions can validate it.
The Frontier Is Correction asks what scientific progress means under that reversal.
More hypotheses and polished reports do not by themselves establish more knowledge.
The book proposes a research programme organized around finding and acting on error.
Its distinctive question is whether reality can still force an automated process to change.
You will encounter technical architecture alongside the institutional authority needed to govern it.
This introduction explains why that combination deserves a researcher's attention.

emotionalPlan.purpose: From surprise toward purpose: This introduction explains why that combination deserves a researcher's attention.

title: A claim before evidence
lines: The introduction follows a plausible claim arriving before its supporting evidence is secure.
A fluent explanation can hide a weak baseline, contamination or a causal mistake.
The problem is not that every machine-generated candidate is worthless.
It is that a candidate and an accepted claim occupy different scientific positions.
The book uses that gap to organize the layers an inquiry needs.
Each layer should expose a failure that polished prose might otherwise conceal.
Reading starts with a familiar research difficulty before widening toward the proposed infrastructure.

title: Reality must be able to object
lines: The philosophical opening treats science as a changing social technology for criticism.
A claim's formal vulnerability is not enough if nobody can force its revision.
The system needs a credible route from detected error to changed understanding.
Tests must be capable of exposing a material mistake, rather than merely repeating procedure.
Different fields build that resistance through different instruments, methods and communities.
The book therefore defends correction without claiming one universal method settles every inquiry.
That foundation explains why its later architecture includes institutions as well as software.

title: Cheap candidates, scarce judgment
lines: When implementation gets cheaper, preparing a research question can become more important.
Assumptions, evaluators and stopping conditions must be explicit before speed amplifies ambiguity.
Finite observations also leave room for different explanations of the same data.
A model's confidence does not remove that problem or establish causal understanding.
The book distinguishes structural limits from engineering problems that better methods might move.
That distinction helps readers avoid both magical optimism and unnecessary resignation.
The practical opportunity is to design the interfaces where uncertainty can become visible.

title: A record that can change
lines: The book proposes an evidence-carrying research object as a durable record of inquiry.
Claims sit beside assumptions, data, code, decisions and reasons for previous changes.
Negative results remain available instead of disappearing behind the final successful narrative.
The paper still matters as a signed, intelligible public view of that record.
A later correction can then identify which claims and dependencies it affects.
This is a proposal about scientific meaning, not merely a different file format.
Chapter three develops why the object needs both versioning and an explicit theory of identity.

emotionalPlan.purpose: From fragmentation toward possibility: Chapter three develops why the object needs both versioning and an explicit theory of identity.

The proposed workbench preserves dependencies so those affected claims can be located.
Only the relevant work should need recomputation, with the reason for change retained.
The example shows why memory must include relationships rather than just accumulated documents.

title: Several ways to be wrong
lines: An executable specification should not freeze research into one unquestioned sequence.
The book describes controlled expansion into rival hypotheses, baselines, controls and replications.
Each branch has a purpose, an evidence role and conditions for stopping.
Generation, search, evaluation and experimentation remain distinct responsibilities within the process.
A useful negative result may redirect the portfolio instead of counting as wasted effort.
The workbench must preserve that possibility through failures and incomplete branches.
Readers see a design space for inquiry, rather than a promise of one final platform.

title: Independent enough to disagree
lines: Asking one model to criticize its own answer does not create independent evidence.
Different prompts can still share data, code, incentives and the same blind spots.
The book proposes tracking those dependencies when assessing the strength of criticism.
A proof checker, another implementation or physical replication can provide different kinds of resistance.
Agreement matters only in relation to how that agreement was produced.
Promotion should require appropriate evidence and named authority, not repeated confidence alone.
This distinction gives researchers a concrete way to question impressive multi-agent demonstrations.

title: Remember why a path failed
lines: Scientific memory should preserve why a promising branch was abandoned or revised.
The proposed operational idea atlas compares purpose, mechanism, assumptions, evidence and lineage.
A distant wording match does not by itself establish a novel scientific idea.
Nor does a close resemblance prove historical influence between researchers.
The book makes these separate relations explicit in its account of comparison.
It then asks whether structured representations outperform strong, simpler retrieval baselines.
That experimental question keeps an ambitious memory proposal open to rejection or simplification.

title: No universal oracle
lines: Different scientific domains can support very different amounts of autonomous work.
A formal proof checker rejects invalid proofs within its own stated assumptions.
A physical experiment also depends on instruments, calibration and a model of measurement.
Social inquiry introduces further questions about categories, values and whose experience is absent.
The book preserves a common architecture without pretending these evaluators are interchangeable.
Delegation should therefore depend on the domain and the consequences of failure.
Chapter seven develops those contrasts beyond the familiar demonstration of a coding agent.

title: Who can change the decision
lines: Human governance means more than clicking approval after the important choices are already made.
People must be able to shape purposes, inspect assumptions and stop consequential actions.
A right of appeal needs an authority capable of changing the outcome.
Infrastructure ownership and access also affect whose criticism can receive a hearing.
The book treats these as scientific design questions, not administrative additions.
Its research programme asks how automation can preserve responsible delegation without ceremonial oversight.
That is one reason the volume connects technical systems to a republic of knowledge.

title: Correction has a cost
lines: Every validator and provenance requirement consumes time, computation or scarce expert attention.
The book does not argue that maximum infrastructure always produces better science.
A simpler system may be preferable if it corrects a bounded failure effectively.
Institutions must also avoid rewarding publication volume while making careful negative results professionally costly.
The proposed architecture should be judged by reliable correction and preserved understanding.
Its own assumptions need tests, baselines and observations that could defeat them.
This qualification makes the book useful for evaluating proposals, including its own.

title: An invitation to investigate
lines: The final chapter turns the preceding principles into researchable technology families.
It connects proposed artifacts to missing capabilities, evaluator regimes and failure conditions.
Some projects concern scientific objects and memory, while others concern critics and institutions.
The names and component boundaries remain provisional rather than promises about a finished product.
The reader is invited to compare implementations and reject complexity that adds little value.
The full volume supplies the depth needed to turn that invitation into specific research questions.
Its purpose is to make future work more criticizable before large systems harden around it.
